description: The US State Department's 2013 human rights report found Palestinians tried in Israeli military courts were convicted more than 99% of the time. Other reporting cites 99.7% for West Bank civilians.
energy_note: A court that has essentially one outcome.

aspect: Which makes pleading guilty the rational choice
description: When acquittal is statistically negligible, a plea for a shorter certain sentence beats a trial for a longer near-certain one. The system therefore generates guilty pleas from people who would contest the facts.
Critics argue trying civilians in military tribunals violates international law and routinely disregards due process. The judges, prosecutors and rules all belong to the party that made the arrest.
energy_note: Everyone in the room works for the other side.

aspect: Families often do not learn the charge
description: Families and institutions frequently receive little information regarding the charges, so the household organises around a sentence whose basis it has never been told.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the figure in a US government report
description: The 2013 US State Department human rights report found Palestinians tried in Israeli military courts were convicted more than 99% of the time. The figure comes from the government of Israel's closest ally, not from a critic.
energy_note: Ninety-nine per cent, per the State Department.
